source: I want to create a military rescue helicopter game. the player is the pilot. they have to fly around and look for people stranded on top of buildings or in other areas in a city. the player has to land the helicopter and load the passengers, then take them back to base to get more. the helicopter can hold 8 passengers

answers.ask: How big should the city be - a few blocks or a sprawling skyline?
answers.answer: Use a small city of a few blocks, with enough rooftops and street-level areas to make searching and landing meaningful.

answers.ask: Roughly how many stranded survivors are out at once, and do they respawn?
answers.answer: Have 8 stranded survivors out at a time, matching the helicopter's full capacity; respawn a new group after they are safely returned to base so the rescue loop continues.

## Clarifications resolved
- [author] scale — Q: How big should the city be - a few blocks or a sprawling skyline? A: Use a small city of a few blocks, with enough rooftops and street-level areas to make searching and landing meaningful.
- [author] free — Q: Roughly how many stranded survivors are out at once, and do they respawn? A: Have 8 stranded survivors out at a time, matching the helicopter's full capacity; respawn a new group after they are safely returned to base so the rescue loop continues.

## Enriched image prompt
Create a military helicopter rescue map over a small city of a few blocks. Place one clear operations base with a helicopter landing pad at the edge of the city. Build a compact cluster of exterior buildings in varied but manageable heights, leaving rooftop pads, broad flat roofs, street-level clearings, and small open lots where a helicopter can land safely. Distribute exactly eight visible stranded-survivor sites across a mix of rooftops and ground-level areas, each with enough unobstructed approach and loading space. Keep the open air above and between buildings as the primary play space, with clear visual routes back to the base and no sprawling skyline beyond the frame.

## Genre
The dominant genre is Simulation, canonical slug `simulation`, because the player operates a helicopter through a repeatable search, landing, passenger-loading, and return task.

## Shape and preset
Use `volume-open-air`, taken by Simulation's Aircraft Operation preset, for flight through open city airspace with discrete rooftops, clearings, and a base pad to land on. Match the Aircraft Operation preset, retaining its task sites and operations hub while dropping unrequested progression gates.

## Config requirements
Use `social-hub` as the compact military operations base and landing pad. Use `trigger-task` for visible rescue loading sites and the base return point. Use universal `settlement-density` for the small city block cluster and `npc-population` for exactly eight stranded survivors and the ground they occupy.

## Layout requirements
Place exactly eight rescue `trigger-task` TriggerZones across rooftop and street-level landing sites, one for each active survivor, plus one return TriggerZone on the base helipad. Place the layout half of `npc-population` as exactly eight survivor positions tied to those sites. New survivor groups appearing after return and the helicopter's eight-passenger capacity are gameplay state; the layout preserves eight simultaneous sites.

## Layout components
Create one operations-base zone with one helipad, one small city of a few blocks, multiple exterior buildings of varied heights, rooftop landing areas, street clearings, open lots, exactly eight rescue sites, and navigable airspace between all sites and the base. Use the city edge as the boundary and frame the base, full block cluster, and varied landing elevations clearly.

## Render order
Use `isometric`: render the city heights, rooftop landing sites, base, and airspace composition first, then derive the top-down view; the isometric image is authoritative because safe vertical approaches matter more than strict ground-route topology.

## Scale, theme, and pipeline cost
Use medium scale, driven by a few city blocks with legible rooftop and street-level rescue sites. The theme is modern military urban rescue. Use `CHECK` because helicopter play occupies a volumetric airspace; the compact skyline should remain acceptable unless its height layers self-occlude.

options.text: A compact military operations base with a helicopter landing pad at the city edge.
Rescue loading sites at each survivor location and a base return point on the helipad.
A small city cluster of a few blocks.
Exactly eight stranded survivors positioned at rescue sites (mix of rooftops and ground-level areas).

layout_placement.text: Rescue TriggerZones: eight at rooftop and street-level landing sites (one per active survivor), plus one return TriggerZone on the base helipad.
Survivor positions: exactly eight survivor positions tied to the eight rescue sites.

layout.composition: Frame the base at the edge of the city with its helipad clearly visible, and include the full compact block cluster with varied building heights so rooftop landing areas, street-level clearings/open lots, and the open airspace between sites and the base are all legible; no sprawling skyline beyond the frame.

zones.name: operations-base
zones.role: Military operations base and helicopter landing/return point.
zones.where: At the edge of the city.

zones.name: small-city-cluster
zones.role: A few city blocks of exterior buildings with rooftop pads, broad flat roofs, street-level clearings, and open lots for helicopter landings; hosts rescue sites.
zones.where: Adjacent to the operations base, forming the main framed area.

zones.name: navigable-airspace
zones.role: Primary play space for helicopter flight above and between buildings, with clear visual routes back to base.
zones.where: Above and between buildings, spanning between all rescue sites and the base.

layout.terrain: Urban ground with exterior buildings of varied but manageable heights; rooftop landing areas, street-level clearings, and small open lots; open air above/between buildings is the primary play space.

props.name: helicopter landing pad / helipad
props.where: In the operations base at the city edge.

props.name: exterior buildings (varied manageable heights)
props.where: Across the compact cluster of a few city blocks.

props.name: rooftop landing areas / broad flat roofs
props.where: On building rooftops throughout the city cluster.

props.name: street-level clearings and small open lots (safe landing spots)
props.where: At street level throughout the city cluster.

props.name: visible stranded-survivor sites
props.where: Distributed across a mix of rooftops and ground-level areas.

layout.boundary: Use the city edge as the boundary; keep any skyline beyond the few blocks out of frame.

render.why: Safe vertical approaches and landing readability matter more than strict ground-route topology.

notes: Layout requirements did not specify explicit placement 'where' rules beyond 'across rooftop and street-level landing sites' and 'tied to those sites'; 'where' left empty per schema rule.
Option `trigger-task` is listed as visible=true because the blob explicitly calls for 'visible rescue loading sites' (despite TriggerZones also being placed in layout).
